description: This bar chart illustrates the GLUE Performance of various fine-tuning methods when applied to two different RoBERTa model sizes: “base” (represented by blue bars) and “large” (represented by orange bars), as indicated in the legend titled “RoBERTa Size.” The vertical y-axis, labeled “GLUE Performance,” ranges from approximately 85 to 89, with tick marks at intervals of 1. The horizontal x-axis, labeled “Fine-tuning Method,” lists seven categories: a grayed-out placeholder (likely representing a baseline or full fine-tuning), followed by “Adaptor,” “LoRA,” “BitFit,” “S₁-model,” “S₄-model,” and “S₅-model.” For each fine-tuning method, two bars are shown side-by-side, comparing the performance of the base and large models. The chart reveals that for most methods, the large model consistently outperforms the base model. Notably, the “S₅-model” achieves the highest GLUE performance overall, with the large version reaching approximately 89.2, while the base version scores around 87.0. The “LoRA” method also shows strong performance, with the large model reaching approximately 89.0 and the base model around 86.7. In contrast, “BitFit” and “S₁-model” show lower performance, with both base and large models scoring around 85.5–85.7. The “Adaptor” method shows a significant gap between base (~85.3) and large (~88.2). The “S₄-model” achieves around 86.2 for base and 87.6 for large. The grayed-out bar, likely representing full fine-tuning, shows a base model performance of approximately 85.3 and a large model performance of approximately 85.7, suggesting that some parameter-efficient methods (like LoRA and S₅-model) can surpass full fine-tuning in performance, especially with the large model.
